items.t: The foundation is laid: Psanctuary Church gets a home on GitHub
items.s: Psanctuary Church now has a quiet, honest home on GitHub: an organization profile, an entry portal at psanctuarychurch.github.io, and this changelog and library. None of it replaces psanctuary.org. It's a place to keep the church's technical work in the open as it grows.

items.s: Why the source behind this site stays private, and how only the finished pages ever get published.
items.x: TL;DR: Everything you're reading is written in a private repository. A small automated job builds the site, throws the source away, and publishes only the finished pages. If a file isn't on an explicit list of what's allowed out, the publish stops. How it works, step by step Two repositories, one direction There are two repositories behind this site: 1. changelog astro (private): the markdown entries, the library docs, and the site's code. 2. changelog astro public (public): only the finished HTML pages, which GitHub Pages serves. Nothing ever flows from public back to private, and nobody edits the public one by hand. What happens on every update When a new entry is saved to the private repo
